title: Australian bank accounts
objective: Compare transaction, savings and offset accounts, bonus-interest conditions, and the Financial Claims Scheme guarantee

sources.name: APRA: Financial Claims Scheme for banks, building societies and credit unions

q.prompt: True or false: if an Australian bank collapsed, you could lose every dollar in your savings account.
q.explanation: The Government's Financial Claims Scheme protects deposits up to {{fcsLimit}} per person at each authorised Australian bank.

q.prompt: Which account usually pays the **least** interest?

options.why: Savings accounts are designed to pay more, often with conditions.
Term deposits usually pay more in return for locking money away.

q.explanation: Transaction accounts are built for spending, with a debit card and easy access, so they pay little or no interest.

screens.title: Three accounts, three jobs
screens.body: A **transaction account** is for daily spending, with a debit card and little interest. A **savings account** pays more but may have conditions. An [[offset account]] is a transaction account linked to a home loan: its balance reduces the loan balance you're charged interest on.

screens.title: Bonus interest has conditions
screens.body: Many savings accounts pay a low **base rate**, plus a **bonus rate** only in months you meet every condition. Miss one and you get the base rate. Read the conditions, not just the headline.

lines: Bonus: +4.00% p.a. if you deposit $1,000+ and don't withdraw

screens.title: The government guarantee
screens.body: The [[Financial Claims Scheme]] protects deposits up to **{{fcsLimit}} per account holder, per bank**, at banks, building societies and credit unions authorised by APRA. It covers transaction, savings and term deposit accounts and separate offset accounts. APRA aims to pay within {{fcsPayoutDays}}.

screens.title: Worked example: Dan's offset
screens.body: Dan has a home loan and keeps his savings in the linked offset account. Assume a 6% p.a. loan rate.

lines: Unlike savings interest, that saving isn't taxed as income

q.prompt: Match each account to its main job.
pairs: Earning interest on money set aside
q.hint: Think about what each account is designed to do best.
q.explanation: Transaction accounts are for spending, savings accounts earn interest, and offsets cut what your loan costs.

q.prompt: Kim's account pays the bonus rate if she deposits $1,000+ and makes no withdrawals that month. She deposits $1,200 but withdraws $50 for a gift. What rate does she earn?

options.text: Base plus bonus, since she deposited enough
options.why: She has to meet every condition. One withdrawal loses the bonus.
Bonus rates are usually all or nothing for the month.

q.hint: Check both conditions, not just one.
q.explanation: The $50 withdrawal broke a condition, so only the base rate applies. Keeping spending money elsewhere helps.

q.prompt: Grace has $300,000 in savings, all at one Australian bank. How much is **not** covered by the Financial Claims Scheme?
q.hint: The limit is {{fcsLimit}} per person, per bank.
q.explanation: $300,000 − {{fcsLimit}} = $50,000 above the limit at that bank.

q.prompt: Dan wants his savings to cut his home loan interest. Tap the account they should sit in.
q.explanation: Money in the offset reduces the loan balance used to calculate interest, so it works hardest there.

q.prompt: Priya's home loan is $520,000 and her offset holds $25,000. Interest is charged on what balance?
q.explanation: $520,000 − $25,000 = $495,000. Every dollar in the offset lowers the balance interest is charged on.

q.prompt: Max has $200,000 at one bank and $200,000 at a different, unrelated bank. All $400,000 is within the Financial Claims Scheme limit.
q.explanation: The limit applies per account holder at each bank, so $200,000 at each of two separate banks is all within it.

q.prompt: Where should each pot of money live?
q.explanation: Money you'll spend soon sits in transaction; money you're building up sits in savings, where withdrawals don't cost you the bonus.

screens.title: Check your setup
screens.body: Look at your accounts. Is your savings money earning the best rate your bank offers, and do you meet the bonus conditions each month?
screens.action: Check your savings account's **bonus conditions** and whether you met them last month.

bullets: Transaction for spending, savings for interest, offset to cut loan interest.
Bonus rates need every condition met each month.
Deposits are guaranteed up to {{fcsLimit}} per person, per bank.

reviewBank.prompt: The Financial Claims Scheme limit applies…

options.why: Several accounts at the same bank share one limit per person.
It's per person at each bank, not per household.

reviewBank.explanation: It's {{fcsLimit}} for each account holder at each authorised bank, building society or credit union.

reviewBank.prompt: Loan balance $400,000, offset balance $40,000. On what balance is interest charged?
If you miss one bonus condition, most accounts still pay part of the bonus rate.
reviewBank.explanation: Bonus rates are usually all or nothing each month: miss a condition and you get the base rate.

reviewBank.prompt: Which account is linked to a home loan to reduce its interest?

options.why: A term deposit locks money away for a fixed rate; it isn't linked to a loan.
A plain transaction account isn't linked to any loan.

reviewBank.explanation: An offset account's balance is subtracted from the loan balance when interest is worked out.
